ReSaverHelper 2: fix crash when the game is busy

A main-thread task captured the request's stack by reference. When the
game stalled longer than the 3 s wait, the request gave up, its stack was
gone, and the task wrote into it when the game finally ran it (crash in
std::string assignment after a 12 s stall). Tasks now own their data
(values and shared_ptr copies), the wait is 30 s, and a set-stage request
that times out reports 'queued' instead of failing.

Rollouts: play to the game's end once the bag is empty, instead of stopping at a leaf

The leaf network trains only on turns that began with tiles in the bag, so a
leaf reached with the bag empty is outside its training rows. With both racks
known and nothing to draw, the hasty playout is deterministic: the exact
value an endgame-trained leaf would only approximate. The kernel and the CPU
reference keep playing after their two plies while the bag is empty; two
scoreless turns in a row end such a game as six would.

Keep the screensaver away while a Steam game window is open (#36)

The stock rule only inhibits idle for fullscreen windows. Games drop out
of fullscreen during launches, intros and DLSS host restarts, and wheel
or pad input does not reset the keyboard/mouse idle timer, so NFSU2 could
hit the screensaver mid-session. Inhibit idle for every steam_app_*
window instead; "focus" would lapse whenever another monitor has focus.

fix: test the LockedHandle before dereferencing it in the game bindings (#127)

Unwrap returns a LockedHandle whose pointer is null when the receiver is
not a wrapper of the class (a method or getter lifted onto a foreign
object; V8 14 has no AccessorSignature to stop that). Every game-handle
binding went straight to `if (!*data)`, dereferencing that null pointer:
an overnight bot run crashed in Unit.getState with a read of 0x8.

Test `!data || !*data` (and `data && *data`) everywhere, so such a call
returns undefined / false like a unit that no longer exists.
